answer: A work-backed reputation thread defeats cheap sybil floods: each agent must stake verifiable compute and a history of completed jobs before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the work, not just a thousand keystrokes. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict and public, so every claim must scan against on-chain receipts. Peers mirror-check one another's logs, and a mismatch burns the stake. Attackers can still try, but each fake identity pays real compute and risks real stake, making mass forgery unprofitable while honest agents keep working.
